title: Saffron and the Secret Garden
markdown:
The beach was very blue, like a robin’s egg. The waves whispered secrets to the sand. A little seal named Saffron lived there. Saffron was soft and white like the moon on the water. Her eyes were dark and shiny, like little black stones. She loved the warm sun kissing her belly. She loved her collection of shiny pebbles, kept safe in a cozy hollow. But sometimes, when something new came along, Saffron would wiggle her little nose and hide behind her favourite smooth grey stone. It felt safe there.

Her very best friend was a fluffy koala named Kiki. Kiki had ears like soft velvety cushions. Her nose was perfectly black and round, like a ripe blueberry. Kiki loved to eat sweet juicy leaves from tall trees. Then she would take a big nap in the sunny leaves. Kiki wasn’t shy about new things. She would just yawn a sleepy yawn, stretch her arms, and climb right up, no matter what it was.

One breezy afternoon the sky was a big soft blue with fluffy white clouds floating by like lazy sheep. Saffron and Kiki were playing near Farmer McGregor’s pumpkin patch. The pumpkins were big and round, like huge orange balls all over the green field. Their skin felt a little bumpy.

“Look, Saffron,” Kiki chirped, voice like happy rustling leaves. “This pumpkin is wobbling. It looks like it has a wiggly tummy.”

Saffron waddled closer. She slid over the grass. One big pumpkin was wobbling, as if it had a tummy ache. Underneath, a stone in the dirt looked wobbly too. It wasn’t settled.

“Oh my,” Saffron whispered, whiskers twitching. A new kind of wobbly.

Kiki gave a gentle push with her paws. Saffron nudged with her wet nose. The wobbly stone moved. With a soft scrape it shifted just enough to show a dark opening underneath.

“A secret tunnel. How fun.” Kiki’s big round eyes got wide.

Saffron waited a little bit. Tunnels could be dark. What if there were bumpy things? But Kiki was already peeking in, head tilted, nose twitching.

“It smells like dirt,” Kiki called, a little muffled. “Like damp moss after soft rain and sleepy flowers dreaming.”

Saffron wriggled her nose. The smell was actually nice, like the earth after a summer shower. Kiki was right there. Saffron took a deep breath and wriggled in after her friend.

The tunnel wasn’t long — like three big bounces. Soon they tumbled into a garden. A sad garden. Flowers drooped. Colourful petals curled up. Leaves on the bushes looked tired and faded. No happy bees buzzed. It was as if the garden had forgotten how to be bright and cheerful.

“Oh, Saffron,” Kiki said softly. Fluffy ears drooped. “It looks so lonely. Like it forgot how to smile.”

Saffron looked around. The wilting flowers made her feel a little sad too. Then her sharp eyes saw something. Sunny sunshine wanted to shine, but thick tangled vines covered everything, a big heavy blanket. The poor flowers and leaves were hidden in the shade.

“The garden needs sunshine,” Saffron said. A little spark of bravery flickered, warm and bouncy. “And it needs a big drink.”

Kiki looked at her friend. Saffron was suggesting doing something. Saffron, who usually stayed near her pebbles.

“We can help. Kiki, can you help me push these vines away from the sun? Just a little bit?”

Kiki, though small, was strong. She scampered to a thick tangle and began nudging. Saffron used her strong flippers to push away bigger clumps. She made little openings. As they worked, little patches of warm golden sunlight began to fall onto the sleepy plants. A few buds seemed to wiggle, as if waking up.

Saffron felt a little braver as she pushed. She saw a little stream nearby, water sparkling. “We need to bring water.” She remembered how her sleek fur helped her glide through water so easily. She waddled to the stream and showed Kiki how to scoop water with big leaves, little green bowls.

Kiki, with great care, nudged the water-filled leaves toward the roots of the wilting flowers. She gently patted a tiny closed bud, whispering soft words. Saffron watched, heart warmer with each kind thing they did.

As the sunbeams, now able to pour freely, warmed the soil, and the cool clear water trickled down to the thirsty roots, the droopy flowers lifted their heads. Petals unfurled slowly — bright reds like jewels, deep blues like the ocean, shiny greens. Leaves on the bushes plumped up, fresh and happy. Little butterflies, wings like painted silk, fluttered in to visit the newly awakened blooms. The forgotten garden was forgotten no more. It was alive and singing with colour.

Saffron looked at her paws, a little damp, then at Kiki, fur speckled with dew, then at the garden all around them. A warm happy feeling spread through her, warmer than the sun on her belly. She had been a little scared. She had helped. She had stepped out from behind her safe stone.

“We did it, Kiki.”

Kiki yawned a big happy yawn, stretching. “We did. And Saffron, you were very brave. You showed me how to be brave, too.”

From that day on they had a secret garden, their special place. They would often visit, bringing more sunshine by gently moving vines, and more refreshing sips from the stream. Saffron still loved her shiny pebbles, their smooth surfaces comforting. She also loved the way the garden remembered them, and the way Kiki napped in a patch of sun that had not been there before.
